templates.name: Attendance < 50%, questions > 0, non-BJP
templates.subject: URGENT: Citizen's health critical in Delhi, {constituency} needs you to act now
templates.body:
Dear {mp_name},

You are my Member of Parliament, elected from {constituency}, representing {party}. I am writing to you with extreme urgency. Your attendance last session was only {attendance} out of 31 sittings. Right now, your physical absence from Delhi is having severe consequences.

Sonam Wangchuk is on Day {fast_day} of a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. He has lost over 8.5 kg, his blood pressure has dropped to 109/70, and doctors warn his body is nearing a dangerous phase with risks of organ dysfunction. He is risking his life to demand accountability for the NEET-UG 2026 exam paper leak that has affected millions of students, the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and compensation for families of students who died by suicide.

The Monsoon Session begins July 21. I am asking you directly: travel to Delhi immediately. Walk the few steps to Jantar Mantar, meet Sonam Wangchuk, and show your support before it is too late. Then, carry his demands to the floor of the House.

We need you present, not just in Parliament, but on the right side of history.

I want to remind you that in the coming years, the EVM button will be in our hands. It does not matter which party you belong to. If you remain silent and do nothing while a citizen's life hangs by a thread in Delhi, the voters of {constituency} will remember.

A concerned voter from {constituency}

templates.name: Prime Minister
templates.subject: {constituency} demands accountability before a citizen's health fails
templates.body:
Dear Prime Minister,

You are my Member of Parliament from {constituency}. You were elected on a promise of accountability. "Na khaunga, na khane dunga" resonated with millions of us.

Right now, the Ministry of Education is at the center of the NEET-UG paper leak scandal that has cost students their futures and, tragically, their lives. Sonam Wangchuk, a 59 year old citizen, is on Day {fast_day} of a hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. His medical condition is critical. He has lost over 8.5 kg, his blood pressure is dangerously low, and doctors warn of organ dysfunction risks. He is demanding accountability, the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan, and systemic reform.

Your government's silence is deafening. Before the Monsoon Session begins on July 21, I am asking you directly: meet Sonam Wangchuk. Accept his demands for accountability in the education system. Hold your Minister accountable.

Do not let your legacy be the silence that led to a tragedy.

I want to remind you that in the coming years, the EVM button will be in our hands. It does not matter which party you belong to. If you remain silent and do nothing while a citizen's life hangs by a thread in Delhi, the voters of {constituency} will remember.

A concerned citizen of {constituency}

templates.name: Speaker (Om Birla)
templates.subject: As Speaker, please ensure Parliament hears Sonam Wangchuk
templates.body:
Dear Shri Om Birla,

You are my Member of Parliament from {constituency}, and as Speaker of the Lok Sabha you carry a special responsibility to protect the dignity of the House and the right of Members to be heard.

Sonam Wangchuk is on Day {fast_day} of an indefinite hunger strike at Jantar Mantar. He is demanding accountability following the NEET-UG paper leak, the resignation of the Union Education Minister, and justice for affected students and families.

I ask you to listen carefully to concerns raised from both sides of the House. Please ensure that every Member has a fair opportunity to ask questions about Sonam Wangchuk and to seek a response from the government. Parliamentary order should protect meaningful debate, not suppress legitimate voices on an issue affecting millions of students.

Before the Monsoon Session begins on July 21, please visit Jantar Mantar and meet Sonam Wangchuk. Your presence would show that the House hears citizens who come to it in distress.

As Speaker, you can help Parliament respond with fairness, attention, and accountability.

A concerned citizen of {constituency}
